title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is an isolated fragment of crystalline Dieudonné theory applied to Lubin–Tate formal groups. The neighbouring pages are unrelated: they are Bourbaki-style text on vector bundles.

Setting (most plausible reading):
- K is a finite extension of Q_p, A its ring of integers, π a uniformizer.
- G is a formal A-module of A-height 1 and dimension 1 over A (a Lubin–Tate group), or the corresponding Barsotti–Tate group with A-action.
- M is a Dieudonné-type lattice attached to G, with dual M̌. Over K, M_K carries the Hodge filtration (ω_G ⊂ M_K).
- \mathcal{L} is a line determined by the A-action (an eigen-line or period line).
- Ω is a rank-1 A-lattice, probably built from the Tate module or periods, and Ω̌ is its dual.

Step 1. The preceding (missing) page recovered the Hodge filtration of M̌_K (equivalently M_K) from \mathcal{L}. Grothendieck concludes this gives a uniqueness theorem up to isogeny. In modern terms: the filtered Dieudonné module, rationally, is forced by the A-action, so all such G are isogenous. He explicitly notes it gives neither existence nor uniqueness up to isomorphism, for which one must refer to Lubin–Tate.

Step 2. Two lattices in one line. The tangent space t_G and Ω̌ are both rank-1 A-lattices in the same 1-dimensional K-vector space. Hence, once π is chosen, t_G = π^α Ω̌ for a unique α ∈ Z; dually Ω = π^α ω_G. The integer α (the valuation of the comparison index) depends only on A. He says it is 'easy to see' and leaves it as some function of A. The natural candidate is the valuation of the different of A/Z_p, possibly up to sign or shift.

Step 3. Second comparison. Over K one has D*(G)_K ≅ M_K ≅ Ω ⊗_{Z_p} K, so the absolute Dieudonné crystal D*(G) (evaluated on A) and M are two integral lattices in the same K-space. He asks whether they coincide, as they do in a special case (illegible: 'existence of parameters ... on πA'). Coincidence would force α = 0, and the question depends only on A, not on π.

Purpose: to test whether the absolute crystalline Dieudonné theory of the underlying p-divisible group recovers the A-linear (Lubin–Tate / relative) structure integrally. It does rationally. Integrally the discrepancy is measured by α, which should be governed by ramification of A/Z_p.
errors: No outright error is visible. 'α = function of A alone, as one easily sees' is asserted without proof.

If the lattices coincided in general, α would be 0. For ramified A one expects α ≠ 0 (a different-type discrepancy), so the answer to his question is presumably negative in general. He leaves it open.
The tensor Ω ⊗_{Z_p} K is dimensionally odd if Ω is a rank-1 A-module: it gives [K:Q_p] dimensions over K. Possibly ⊗_A was meant, or M_K denotes an eigen-component. The page is too terse to decide.

ideas.what: Using the Hodge filtration on the Dieudonné crystal, determined by the A-action, to prove uniqueness up to isogeny of Lubin–Tate formal A-modules
ideas.modern_name: Filtered Dieudonné module / crystalline Dieudonné theory of Barsotti–Tate groups with O-action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (crystalline Dieudonné theory, 1970), Messing (1972), Mazur–Messing; Lubin–Tate (1965) for existence and uniqueness
ideas.where_published: General framework in Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux' (ICM 1970) and Montréal lectures (1974). This specific Lubin–Tate application is not known to be there.

ideas.what: Comparison of two rank-1 A-lattices, t_G versus the dual of a period/Tate lattice Ω, differing by π^α with α depending only on A
ideas.modern_name: Integral comparison / Hodge–Tate period lattice of Lubin–Tate groups; discrepancy given by the different
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1967, p-divisible groups); Fontaine (1982, 'Formes différentielles et modules de Tate'); Colmez (periods of CM abelian varieties)

ideas.what: Question whether the absolute Dieudonné crystal D*(G) and the A-linear Dieudonné lattice M coincide, depending only on A
ideas.modern_name: Relative (strict O-module) Dieudonné theory versus absolute Dieudonné theory; O-displays
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1976, formal A-modules); Faltings (2002, 'Group schemes with strict O-action'); Ahsendorf–Cheng–Zink (O-displays)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly raises the integral comparison between the absolute Dieudonné crystal of a Lubin–Tate group and an A-linear Dieudonné lattice. He notes that equality would force α = 0 and that the question depends only on A. This prefigures the later theory of strict O-modules, where the absolute and relative Dieudonné modules differ integrally, by a discrepancy tied to ramification/different. He did not pursue it; the later resolution came independently (Faltings, Ahsendorf–Cheng–Zink).
missed.quote: On peut se demander si ces sous-réseaux sont les mêmes ... ce qui impliquerait évidemment α = 0.. Cela ne dépend pas du choix de π, mais seulement de A
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical rather than new mathematics. It shows Grothendieck around 1970 already identified the integral mismatch between absolute crystalline and O-linear Dieudonné theory, well before Drinfeld and Faltings. The answer is now known, so the page has little research value.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a short, partly illegible exploratory note applying the new crystalline Dieudonné theory to Lubin–Tate groups. It correctly isolates an integral lattice-comparison question (the α exponent, likely the different) that was later answered in Fontaine's and Faltings' work. It is mildly interesting as a precursor, but contains no finished new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Cela donne bien th. d'unicité à isogénie près' — the image reads 'Cela donne bien th. d'unicité à isogénie près', consistent with the transcription.
Crossed-out text after 'isomorphes,' and the struck 'On peut' before 'où α ∈ Z' are deletions in the manuscript.
In 't_G = π^{α} Ω̌' the exponent has a smudged correction (possibly a sign was changed); read t_G = π^{α} Ω̌, Ω = π^{α} ω_G.
'α = fn [?] de A' probably reads 'α = fn de A tous seuls', i.e. a function of A alone.
The subscript on D*(G) in 'D*(G)_K' looks like a tilde-decorated π or K in the image (D*(G)_{π̃}?). Uncertain.
'comme dans le cas où ∃ param. de ... sur πA' is partly illegible; possibly 'paramètres de Lubin–Tate'.
